📚 Tokenized Real Estate Explained

• Most tokenized real estate structures use a legal entity that owns the property, with tokens representing shares in that entity.

• Fractional ownership can lower investment minimums, but liquidity for those tokens is still limited in practice.

• Property management, maintenance and legal title still function largely as they do in traditional real estate.
